basis: Eye, brain and skin malformations define the syndrome; calvarial defects and rib abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting skeletal involvement.
Adenomatous colorectal polyposis defines NTHL1-related FAP; associated extraintestinal cancers are separately diagnosed diseases and cancer risks.
Immune-mediated granulomatous inflammation directly affects the heart; this organ-specific concept does not establish other damaged organs.
Carcinoma originates in salivary gland acinar epithelium; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Microspherophakia is an intrinsic lens malformation; the unspecified associated hernia does not establish damage to another covered organ.
Keratoconus with acute corneal hydrops directly affects the cornea.
Malignancy of the lower lip, classified here as an oral cavity site.
An inherited Alzheimer disease subtype defined by cerebral neurodegeneration and dementia.
Cardiac, skeletal and skin abnormalities define MASS; myopia is a characteristic common feature (about >=30%); dural ectasia alone does not establish neurologic injury.
Acute myeloid malignancy of marrow and blood defined by chromosome 3 inversion.
Malignant precursor T cells affect marrow and blood; the supplied leukemia/lymphoma concept also encompasses lymphoblastic lymphoma.
Combined immunodeficiency with hypogammaglobulinemia and skeletal anomalies defines the syndrome; no additional organ damage is established.
Peripheral nerve damage defines the disease; the causative endocrine disorder is a separately identifiable underlying condition.
Dorsal midbrain gaze-control dysfunction causes the ocular motor signs; intrinsic damage to the eye is not established.
Congenital abnormalities of coronary artery origin, course or structure.
Combined complete atrioventricular septal defect and tetralogy of Fallot are structural cardiac malformations.
Cancer of uterine supporting ligaments is reproductive; these ligaments are outside the locomotor musculoskeletal axis despite the broad ontology parent.
Congenital myopathy and contractures with cerebral and retinal hemorrhage define the syndrome; respiratory insufficiency reflects neuromuscular failure, not intrinsic lung injury.
Severe cerebral and renal malformations define MARCH; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 11/11 and arthrogryposis in 12/12 patients.
Pathogenic partial chromosome 13 duplications commonly cause neurodevelopmental impairment; the unspecified interval prevents reliable assignment of other organs.
Carcinoma arises from renal parenchymal or renal pelvic epithelium; metastases are not defining organ involvement.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome; common external-ear dysmorphism does not establish functional injury, and hearing loss occurs in only 5-29%.
Prototheca algal infection; destructive cutaneous lesions occur in roughly 50-70%; bursitis and other systemic sites are less common.
Benign fibro-osseous bone neoplasm, usually mandibular; jawbone origin supports the musculoskeletal axis.
Ectopic endometrial tissue directly occupies and injures the intestine; the affected site is gastrointestinal.
